deepdive.thesis: Jubilant FoodWorks gained pizza market share despite Q4 LFL growth deceleration to 0.2%, driven by conscious reduction in minimum order value to Rs.99 and premium product launches; near-term margin compression from 120 bps energy inflation and labor cost hikes is expected, but structural improvements in gross margin and capex efficiency support 200 bps margin expansion target over two years.

open.item: Board recommended a dividend of INR1.2 per equity share (60% of INR2 face value) for FY2026, amounting to INR791.81 million, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM, in line with the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy and consistent multi-year payment track record.
Popeyes is targeted to achieve restaurant-level profitability by exit-FY27.
The Company targets reducing the drag from emerging businesses on standalone adjusted EBITDA (pre-Ind AS 116) to approximately 100 basis points by the end of FY28, from ~220 bps in FY26.

The Board approved non-renewal of the development and operation rights for the Dunkin' brand in India upon expiry of the current agreement term, as part of disciplined capital allocation and portfolio rationalisation; the transition is being executed in a phased, orderly manner in line with contractual and regulatory requirements.
Standalone Return on Capital Employed (RoCE), at ~18.9% in FY26 on a pre-Ind AS 116 basis, is progressing toward a steady-state target of 20%+.

Capital allocation is expected to remain disciplined, with capex intensity expected to moderate structurally as revenues scale and large supply-chain investments are largely behind; free cash flow generation is expected to strengthen steadily over the next three years.

risks.note: Operations span sourcing, food preparation and service, where food safety hazards or contamination could impact consumer well-being, erode brand reputation/trust, trigger regulatory fines or sanctions, and cause temporary closures, product recalls or supply-chain disruption; financial implications include recall/disposal costs, alternative-supplier costs, penalties, and legal fees/settlements from affected consumers or regulators.

Given the scale of the workforce engaged daily in food preparation, delivery logistics and diverse urban environments, unsafe conditions could raise attrition, harm morale/productivity, damage reputation via negative publicity, and generate medical/rehabilitation/claims costs, insurance premium increases, and fines/litigation for OHS non-compliance.
risks.risk: Employee and delivery-workforce health, safety and wellbeing

risks.note: Maintaining ethical conduct across an increasingly interconnected and scrutinised business environment is flagged as a risk area; perceived ethical lapses could affect organisational culture, regulatory compliance and reputation, with financial implications from legal investigations/lawsuits, fines/penalties and lost sales from negative publicity.

The evolving landscape of ESG frameworks/regulations and changing stakeholder (investor, regulator, community) expectations creates a risk of non-compliance with statutory requirements and negative publicity around sustainable-business practices, with financial implications including legal liabilities, fines/penalties and sales/profitability impact.
risks.risk: ESG framework, environmental and regulatory compliance

risks.note: Increasing reliance on digital ordering, mobile and cloud touchpoints exposes the Company to hacking, ransomware and social-engineering threats that could cause unauthorised disclosure of Company/consumer/employee data, business disruption, financial losses and reputational damage; the Company notes its IT infrastructure aligns with ISO 27001 and the NIST Cyber Security Framework and reported no information security breaches in FY26.
